items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Oscar and I were very close friends

ctx.x: so I can imagine how disjointed -- I never saw it, but I can imagine how -- what a cross patched, messed up thing it must be. Some of it was done in New York, some was done in Hollywood, and then, you know, they just recorded and filmed segments and sewed it together afterwards. They wrote the story afterwards, I think, and fit in all these things. If there was a story. Oh, you asked about Pettiford. Well, we were playing -- in 1943, we were playing the Orpheum Theater in Minneapolis, and Chubby came in and he…

ever seen, but now Chubby comes to me and he says, "Charlie, Oscar ain't making it." I said, "Oh, really?" He said, "No, no, he's not making it." The next day Oscar comes to me and he says, "Charlie, I hate to say this but Chubby ain't making it." And they finally wound up, with Oscar said he couldn't stand it any longer, and I had a contract with Chubby. I said, "There isn't anything I can do, I've got to honor the contract, and if you're unhappy, which I'm very sorry," -- Oscar -- I don't know where he went,…
Yeah. Yeah. Had he -- I know Minneapolis is his home. Had he travelled before that?
